data.narrative:
Magrathea Metals is a Series A climate and energy technology company founded by Alex Grant and Jacob Brown, having raised $100M+ to date. The valuation landscape includes 9 peers in the Climate & Energy sector, comprising 1 public company and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($100M) as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement to subsequent funding rounds yields an implied valuation of $200M. The Peer-Median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable companies within the narrow peer set—while 9 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of three or more comparable datapoints when filtered by stage, timing, and valuation tier. Including all-sector peers would introduce excessive methodological noise.

The triangulated valuation range spans $170M (low) to $230M (high), with a median of $200M. This single-method analysis reflects a meaningful constraint: the frontier-tech climate sector exhibits sparse late-stage public comparables and wide dispersion among private valuations, limiting triangulation robustness. Key uncertainties include technology commercialization risk, capital intensity of scaling, and commodity price volatility. A more precise range would require either near-term funding event data or materially improved comparable density in the subsector.
